scope_entries.finding: pins torch==2.11.0+cu128/torchaudio==2.11.0+cu128 via --extra-index-url .../whl/cu128; its comment justifies this as 'cu128 wheels run on the cu130 host driver via CUDA forward-compatibility (validated on DGX Spark, 580.126.09)' — true but off-axis: forward-compat spans the driver/runtime gap, never synthesizes SASS for an uncompiled arch. The misleading comment is itself in scope, else the pin recurs

downloaded (517MB) and dumped: cuobjdump --list-elf libtorch_cuda.so -> sm_80/sm_90/sm_100/sm_120 only; --list-ptx -> empty. No sm_110 SASS and no PTX to JIT from (and compute_120 PTX could not JIT DOWN to sm_110 anyway). Validated 2026-06-21 on Spark GB10 = sm_121, which sm_120 SASS covers via minor-version compat — that is why this never surfaced

scope_entries.surface: model-gear-vllm-muse container (the live cu130 counter-example on this box)
scope_entries.finding: torch 2.11.0+cu130 with arch list ['sm_80','sm_90','sm_100','sm_110','sm_120'] and device capability (11,0) — cu130 is the Thor-safe line, proven on the target card, and torch-2.11.0+cu130 aarch64 wheels exist on download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130

the lean nvidia/cuda:13.0.1-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu24.04 base exists specifically because NGC pytorch's bundled torchaudio ABI-conflicts with Perth's C extension; Perth is installed --no-deps AFTER torch so it links the cu128 ABI. Moving to cu130 re-opens exactly the question that rationale closes — the repin is not a one-line bump

ROLES = (cortex, senses, muse, embedder, reranker) — stt/tts excluded on the stated premise that they are 'fixed audio sidecars with no machine-dependent vLLM knobs of their own'. #145 does not falsify that comment literally (a torch wheel arch is not a vLLM knob) but collides with its CONCLUSION: Chatterbox IS machine-dependent, just at build time. RoleProfile carries only serving knobs, so there is no build-knob field to hang a per-card pin on

both declare only [roles.cortex|senses|embedder|reranker] serving knobs; neither mentions stt/tts/chatterbox/parakeet at all — confirming the schema exclusion is real in the data, not just the comment. A per-card torch pin would need BOTH a ROLES extension and a new non-vLLM knob class

scope_entries.surface: lobes/templates/fleet/docker-compose.audio.yml build args (the fallback mechanism, if per-card is ever forced)
scope_entries.finding: the chatterbox service already passes build args from env: MODEL_GEAR_VERSION and LOBES_DEV_INDEX_URL: ${GATEWAY_PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL:-}. So an env -> compose -> build-arg path for a torch index URL already has a working precedent and would NOT need new machinery — but it would still need a per-card source for the value, which the profile schema declines to be

every job is runs-on: ubuntu-latest and NO workflow contains a docker build step — the Dockerfile's own header claim ('CI is CPU-only x86 and does NOT build this Dockerfile') is accurate. So nothing in CI can catch a card-wrong pin; only a live boot can. This is why #145 sat undetected behind a green pipeline
